criteria.evidence: Approved retrieval contract limits fields to invoice number and customer name, explicitly supports partial names, and offers Draft/Sent and Date range. It marks number matching, typo/synonym support, counts, and scale Unknown rather than inventing capabilities or metadata.

F2 explicitly leaves Draft plus Sent combination unresolved and says not to assume OR or AND; F3 likewise leaves query/status/date combinations unresolved and requires owner decisions checked against backend support.

The states table separates no matches, successfully established empty corpus, and retrieval failure. F6 proposes individual query/status/date removal with criteria retention, and explicitly says clearing never changes invoices or invoice drafts; acceptance checks preserve unrelated work.

Provides concrete scoped labels, visible criteria, keyboard/status feedback, and acceptance checks conditioned on F1–F5 decisions. Founder additions are explicitly outside approved scope with no controls or data requirements; ranking, performance, and validation are not promised.

Specifies invoice number or customer name with supported partial-name matching and only Draft/Sent status and date range. It does not promise typo correction, synonyms, or number prefix matching, and explicitly omits unsupported counts and scale claims.

D1 blocks multiple-status behavior until product approval and backend confirmation rather than assuming OR. D2 explicitly declines AND across query/status/date and also leaves cross-field matching unresolved.

Separates successful no-match results from a confirmed unfiltered empty list, loading, and failure. It allows query editing/clearing, individual status removal, and date changes while retaining criteria; clear scope explicitly excludes invoice deletion, status changes, and discarded drafts.

Useful current-list presentation, ambiguous-name handling, scoped recovery, and unperformed acceptance checks are supplied. D6 keeps payment status, tags, and saved searches outside scope without placeholders or implied data models; no ranking or SDK is added.

Retrieval contract limits search to invoice number and customer name, states partial customer-name support, and specifies Draft/Sent multi-selection and date range. Other match details, ranking, counts, scale, and date semantics remain Unknown; no new metadata is established.

The status contract explicitly rejects silently implementing OR or AND, while Combined criteria and F3 leave query/filter and cross-filter rules unresolved. F1–F5 are decision dependencies rather than backend defaults.

No-match recovery preserves all criteria and explicitly allows one change without losing the others. Named clearing changes retrieval only, never invoices or saved invoice work; confirmed empty permitted corpus and retrieval failure have separate conditions and feedback.

Offers proposed interactions within existing Invoices, meaningful accessible feedback, and concrete checks after F1–F5 decisions, with all verification explicitly unperformed. Founder additions stay outside scope with no implementation commitments; existing access enforcement remains unverified.

Contract uses only invoice number/customer name search, supported partial names, Draft/Sent multi-select, and date range. Unknown number matching, field combination, date semantics, counts, and dataset size are not filled with assumptions; it forbids unapproved columns and ranking.
F2 requires approval for both selected statuses and neither selected, explicitly recognizing OR versus AND as unresolved. F3 says not to silently assume AND across query, status, and date.

The proposed states distinguish no matches from an established accessible empty base list and request failure. Staff can clear search, selected statuses, or date range independently, retaining editable criteria; clearing never deletes invoices or changes their statuses.

Provides scoped labels, pending/applied criteria guidance, invalid-date correction dependent on approved rules, and acceptance checks including accessibility and exit behavior. Payment status/tags/saved searches are excluded from controls, routes, and data models; runtime remains unverified.

Scope table specifies invoice number/customer name, partial customer-name support, Draft/Sent multiple selections, and date range only. Unknown number/date rules, counts, and scale remain unresolved; suggestions, typo correction, query rewriting, and numerical claims are not promised.

D2 explicitly declines assuming OR, AND, or another within-Status interpretation. D3 leaves cross-criteria rules unresolved, and D4 separately identifies defaults and no-selected-status meaning for an approved decision.

Proposed states distinguish a successful no-match query, distinguishable empty underlying list, and failed retrieval. Recovery is user-directed and individual clearing preserves other criteria; clear-all scope is explicit and never record deletion, while invalid dates do not discard unrelated criteria.

Gives concrete scoped presentation and recovery, query/result consistency decisions, and acceptance checks with expected results deferred until rules are approved. Founder additions have no controls/placeholders/data requirements, no new ranking/SDK is added, and runtime/recovery validation is explicitly absent.

Only invoice number and customer name are approved searchable fields, with supported partial names; Status is Draft/Sent multi-select and Date range is the other facet. Match details, ranking, counts, scale, sorting/pagination support, and date interpretation remain unresolved rather than invented.

Within-Status row says not to implement OR or AND without approval, including unresolved no-selection behavior. Combined criteria explicitly declines assuming intersection/AND and requires the owner to approve both combination rules.

No matches retain visible editable query/status/date criteria with scoped removal, preservation of unrelated work, and no automatic relaxation. Empty collection requires established unfiltered emptiness; failures are separately described and preserve criteria as a requirement. Clearing cannot affect invoices, drafts, or selected records.

Provides practical current-list labels, supported recovery and exit, acceptance checks for searches/combinations/states, and proposed accessible feedback. Payment status/tags/saved searches remain later-scope suggestions without placeholders or requirements; no ranking/SDK or validated-findability claim is introduced.
